results.references: - Jelena Diakonikolas and Cristóbal Guzmán. [Lower Bounds for Parallel and Randomized Convex Optimization](https://jmlr.org/papers/volume21/19-771/19-771.pdf). 2020. Complexity: $\Omega(\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon})$ sequential local-oracle calls for randomized algorithms achieving objective gap $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\gamma$, for constant $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and $d=\Omega((LR^2/\varepsilon)^{3/2}\log(LR^2/\varepsilon))$; the oracle can supply exact function values and gradients.

- Yurii E. Nesterov. [A method of solving a convex programming problem with convergence rate O(1/k²)](https://hengshuaiyao.github.io/papers/nesterov83.pdf). 1983. Complexity: $O(1+\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon})$ exact-gradient calls for objective gap at most $\varepsilon$, using Nesterov’s accelerated method with known $L$; no function-value calls are required.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained convex minimization on ℝᵈ with globally L-Lipschitz gradient and a global minimizer xstar satisfying ‖x0−xstar‖≤R.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns ∇f(x). Every history and seed must return the exact gradient; no function values or noisy observations are supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.admissible, HasGradientAt condition; LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvexExpected.lean: spec.Query and spec.Reply.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean space ℝᵈ. All parameters d,L,x0,R,ε are public. Require L,R,ε>0, 262144ε≤LR², and d≥65536(⌊√(LR²/ε)/512⌋+1)⁵.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point in ℝᵈ; its objective gap relative to an attained global minimum is integrable and has integral at most ε.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expected objective gap E[f(output)−f(xstar)]≤ε under the execution probability law, allowing randomized algorithms.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Standard smooth convex exact-gradient optimization with expected objective accuracy; the small-accuracy and large-dimension restrictions specify a lower-bound benchmark regime.
